0.name: Apple___Apple_scab
0.cause: Fungal (Venturia inaequalis). Thrives in cool, wet spring weather.
0.remedy: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn. Prune trees to increase airflow. Apply preventative fungicides (like Captan or copper-based sprays) as buds break in spring.

1.name: Apple___Black_rot
1.cause: Fungal (Botryosphaeria obtusa). Infects dead tissue, often entering through wounds.
1.remedy: Prune out dead or diseased wood. Remove all mummified fruit from the tree and ground. Apply protective fungicides.

2.name: Apple___Cedar_apple_rust
2.cause: Fungal (Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae). Requires two hosts: apple trees and eastern red cedar trees.
2.remedy: Remove nearby red cedar trees if possible. Apply protective fungicides to the apple tree in early spring before spores blow in.

3.name: Apple___healthy
3.remedy: Keep up the good work! Maintain proper watering and pruning schedules.

4.name: Blueberry___healthy
4.remedy: Keep up the good work! Maintain proper watering and pruning schedules.

5.name: Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew
5.cause: Fungal (Podosphaera clandestina). Favored by high humidity and warm temperatures.
5.remedy: Prune to improve air circulation. Apply sulfur-based or potassium bicarbonate sprays. Avoid overhead watering.

6.name: Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy
6.remedy: Keep up the good work! Maintain proper watering and pruning schedules.

7.name: Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray_leaf_spot
7.cause: Fungal (Cercospora zeae-maydis). Spores survive the winter in corn debris left on the soil.
7.remedy: Practice crop rotation. Till the soil to bury infected crop residue. Plant disease-resistant hybrids.

8.name: Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_
8.cause: Fungal (Puccinia sorghi). Spores blow in from warmer climates. Thrives in high humidity and cool temperatures.
8.remedy: Plant rust-resistant varieties. Apply foliar fungicides early in the season if symptoms appear.

9.name: Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight
9.cause: Fungal (Exserohilum turcicum). Overwinters in corn residue.
9.remedy: Crop rotation (1-2 years away from corn). Deep plowing to bury debris. Fungicide applications in severe cases.

10.name: Corn_(maize)___healthy
10.remedy: Keep up the good work! Maintain proper watering and soil health.

11.name: Grape___Black_rot
11.cause: Fungal (Guignardia bidwellii). Flourishes in warm, humid weather.
11.remedy: Remove all mummified grapes. Ensure good canopy management for airflow. Apply preventative fungicides from early spring through mid-summer.

12.name: Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles)
12.cause: Complex of various fungi entering through pruning wounds.
12.remedy: There is no cure once infected. Prevent by avoiding pruning during wet weather and treating pruning wounds with protective pastes. Remove severely infected vines.

13.name: Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spot)
13.cause: Fungal (Pseudocercospora vitis). Occurs late in the season in wet conditions.
13.remedy: Usually does not require aggressive chemical treatment. Improve airflow and spray Bordeaux mixture (copper sulfate) if necessary.

14.name: Grape___healthy
14.remedy: Keep up the good work! Maintain proper canopy management.

15.name: Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening)
15.cause: Bacterial (Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus). Spread by a tiny insect called the Asian citrus psyllid.
15.remedy: No cure. This is a fatal disease. Infected trees must be uprooted and destroyed immediately to prevent the bugs from spreading it to neighboring healthy trees.

16.name: Peach___Bacterial_spot
16.cause: Bacterial (Xanthomonas campestris). Spread by splashing rain and overhead irrigation.
16.remedy: Avoid overhead watering. Apply copper-based bactericides. Maintain tree vigor and prune well for airflow.

17.name: Peach___healthy
17.remedy: Keep up the good work! Maintain proper watering and pruning schedules.

18.name: Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot
18.cause: Bacterial (Xanthomonas campestris). Spread by splashing rain and overhead irrigation.
18.remedy: Avoid overhead watering. Apply copper-based bactericides. Practice crop rotation.

19.name: Pepper,_bell___healthy
19.remedy: Keep up the good work! Maintain proper watering and spacing.

20.name: Potato___Early_blight
20.cause: Fungal (Alternaria solani). Soil-borne and hits older, stressed leaves first.
20.remedy: Practice a 2-3 year crop rotation. Water at the base of the plant to keep leaves dry. Apply copper or chlorothalonil fungicides.

21.name: Potato___Late_blight
21.cause: Water mold (Phytophthora infestans). Extremely fast-spreading in cool, wet weather.
21.remedy: Pull and destroy infected plants immediately (do not compost). Apply protective copper fungicides before infection occurs.

22.name: Potato___healthy
22.remedy: Keep up the good work! Maintain proper crop rotation and soil health.

23.name: Raspberry___healthy
23.remedy: Keep up the good work! Maintain proper watering and pruning schedules.

24.name: Soybean___healthy
24.remedy: Keep up the good work! Maintain proper watering and soil health.

25.name: Squash___Powdery_mildew
25.cause: Fungal. Thrives in dry, warm climates with high humidity around the plant canopy.
25.remedy: Space plants adequately. Apply neem oil, sulfur sprays, or a baking soda/water mixture at the first sign of white spots.

26.name: Strawberry___Leaf_scorch
26.cause: Fungal (Diplocarpon earlianum). Overwinters in dead leaves and spreads via splashing water.
26.remedy: Remove and destroy infected foliage. Ensure good soil drainage and weed control to allow the plants to dry out quickly.

27.name: Strawberry___healthy
27.remedy: Keep up the good work! Maintain proper watering and spacing.

28.name: Tomato___Bacterial_spot
28.cause: Bacterial (Xanthomonas campestris). Spread by splashing rain and overhead irrigation.
28.remedy: Avoid overhead watering. Apply copper-based bactericides. Practice crop rotation.

29.name: Tomato___Early_blight
29.cause: Fungal (Alternaria solani). Soil-borne and hits older, stressed leaves first.
29.remedy: Practice a 2-3 year crop rotation. Water at the base of the plant to keep leaves dry. Apply copper or chlorothalonil fungicides.

30.name: Tomato___Late_blight
30.cause: Water mold (Phytophthora infestans). Extremely fast-spreading in cool, wet weather.
30.remedy: Pull and destroy infected plants immediately (do not compost). Apply protective copper fungicides before infection occurs.

31.name: Tomato___Leaf_Mold
31.cause: Fungal (Passalora fulva). Primarily an issue in high-tunnel or greenhouse environments with poor ventilation.
31.remedy: Increase ventilation, reduce humidity, and avoid wetting the foliage. Apply protective fungicides.

32.name: Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot
32.cause: Fungal (Septoria lycopersici). Spores splash up from the soil onto the lowest leaves.
32.remedy: Apply a thick layer of mulch to prevent soil splashing. Remove the lowest branches so leaves don't touch the dirt. Use fungicidal sprays.

33.name: Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider_mite
33.cause: Pest. Microscopic arachnids that suck sap from the leaves, thriving in hot, dry conditions.
33.remedy: Spray plants with a strong blast of water to dislodge them. Use insecticidal soap, neem oil, or introduce natural predators like ladybugs.

34.name: Tomato___Target_Spot
34.remedy: Improve airflow, avoid overhead irrigation, and apply appropriate broad-spectrum fungicides.

35.name: Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus
35.remedy: No cure. Pull and destroy infected plants. Manage whitefly populations using insecticidal soaps or reflective mulches.

36.name: Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus
36.cause: Viral. Highly contagious; mechanically transmitted by human hands, tools, or even tobacco products.
36.remedy: No cure. Destroy infected plants. Wash hands with soap thoroughly, sterilize garden tools, and avoid smoking near tomato plants.

37.name: Tomato___healthy
37.remedy: Keep up the good work! Maintain proper watering and spacing.
